reader_questions: Do I enter a Korean city bus through the front or rear door?
When should I press the stop bell, and will the bus stop automatically?
Must I tap my transportation card when getting off if I am not transferring?
Can a tourist pay cash, or are Korean city buses cashless?
How do transfer discounts, time limits, and same-route exclusions work?
What should I do when the card reader says the balance is insufficient?
Which seats should a visitor leave for older, pregnant, injured, or disabled passengers?
Can I carry coffee or takeout food onto a Seoul bus?
Which map app gives foreign visitors live bus arrivals and boarding guidance?

sources.name: Seoul Metropolitan Government Bus Guide and Fares
factual_notes: Seoul transfer rules require tapping when getting off and normally boarding the next service within 30 minutes, extended to 60 minutes at night.
Transfers are accepted up to four times for five boardings, but the same bus or same route is excluded.

The page lists adult card fares of KRW 1,500 for trunk and branch buses, KRW 3,000 for rapid buses, KRW 2,500 for owl buses, and KRW 1,200 for local buses, while warning that distance charges can apply.
Prepaid transportation cards are sold at convenience stores and charging stations.

sources.name: VISITKOREA City Bus Guide
factual_notes: Most Korean city buses use the front door for boarding and the rear door for exiting.
Cashless buses are expanding; all city buses in Incheon, Daegu, and Gwangju are described as cashless, with many Seoul routes also cashless.
A transportation card is required for transfer discounts; cash payment does not receive the transfer benefit.
Transfer rules vary by city, and the page gives Busan as an example with fewer transfers than Seoul.

sources.name: VISITKOREA Transportation Cards
factual_notes: Tmoney and EZL cards can be purchased and recharged at convenience stores nationwide without opening a Korean bank account.
The page lists general Tmoney card purchase prices around KRW 3,000 to KRW 5,000, separate from the stored balance.
Physical Climate Card short-term passes are limited to covered Seoul services, so route coverage must be checked before relying on one.

sources.name: Seoul Metropolitan Government Public Transportation Guide
factual_notes: The official three-step sequence is prepare the card and bus information, enter at the front and tap, then press the bell, tap at the rear reader, and exit through the back.
The stop bell should be pressed before arrival at the destination stop.
Naver Map, Kakao Map, TOPIS, and stop displays can provide live bus location and arrival information.
Using multiple mobile transit apps can cause double payment or transfer errors.

sources.name: Seoul Rules for Food Carried on City Buses
factual_notes: Drivers may refuse spill-prone or unpackaged food intended for consumption on board.
Disposable cups, open drinks, and leak-prone takeout can be prohibited, while sealed bottles, closed cans, sealed tumblers, and securely boxed food are listed as acceptable examples.
A passenger consuming prohibited items may be asked to leave.

sources.name: Official Seoul Travel Bus Page
factual_notes: Seoul has blue trunk, green branch, local, yellow circulation, and red rapid bus types with different route roles.
Cashless operations have expanded and tourists are directed to buy and recharge a transportation card at convenience stores or station machines.
English-capable route apps are recommended for visitors.

sources.name: NAVER Map Multilingual Public Transit Guide
factual_notes: NAVER Map supports Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese.
Its public-transit features include real-time arrival information, boarding and alighting guidance, subway maps, and alternative routes.
The company provides a multilingual usage guide aimed at foreign visitors.
